Subject: Actionable SLO runbook & reserved pool sizing

Hi Mike — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + a short, actionable plan so we can size the dedicated pool and lock the pilot timeline. TL;DR: we think a 3-node reserved pool (A100x2 equiv) will hit your 99th%-tile streaming SLOs at the target concurrency; see attached SLO matrix and pricing draft.

Key points from call ( AtlasCare production chat workload ):
- Latency target: 95% < 120ms per streaming token, 99% < 250ms for short requests (<= 128 tokens).
- Peak concurrent user streams: 140 concurrent active streams (each ~1 req/sec average token generation).
- Throughput: sustained ~180K tokens/minute during peak windows (burst to 260K tokens/min).
- Model: open-llama-70B variant (quantized) for deterministic outputs; will recommend an natively-optimized variant for streaming.

Preliminary sizing recommendation (reserved pool):
- Baseline pilot: 3 reserved instances (mix of 2xA100-80GB equivalence). This gives headroom for KV-cache and burst.
- If you need aggressive tail-latency (99.9%), plan for +1 instance or fallback routing to a higher-priority pool.

Pilot scope & success criteria:
- Duration: 3 weeks pilot (2 weeks testing + 1 week production shadow).
- Workloads: replay your representative prompt set (you shared 12k prompts) and live shadowing with 5% production traffic.
- SLO gates: 95% < 120ms and 99% < 250ms for streaming tokens; error rate <0.5%; no more than 3 fallbacks per hour.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the pilot dates (we suggested Jul 11 start).
2) You share the final prompt set and a short token distribution CSV.
3) Internal sizing confirm by our infra team (cc'd Soojin & Ben).
4) We'll spin up the reserved pool, run bench + streaming smoke, and share a short runbook for ops handoff.

Attachments: slo_matrix_v1.xlsx (SLOs + throughput sims), pilot_pricing_draft.pdf

Thanks — I can hop on a 20-min follow-up to walk the matrix with your SREs if helpful.

—

Karthik — thanks for the concise plan. A few quick clarifications before we commit to the pilot: 

1) Streaming details: our streams are long-tail — a lot of short bursts plus occasional long sessions (up to ~800 tokens). Will the recommendation above handle those long sessions without pushing the 99th% over the target?
2) Cold-start behavior: how much of an impact should we expect on the first few requests when a model shard is cold (e.g., after autoscale down to zero)?
3) Fallback behavior: if we route to a smaller quantized variant during capacity pressure, what is the expected latency delta and how do you measure quality regression?

We can confirm Jul 11 for the pilot start but want the answers to the above so our infra lead can sign off. Also can you drop a one-page ops runbook (steps to validate SLOs + who to call for escalation)?

—Mike

Mike — thanks for the quick review. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) Long sessions (800 tokens): on our 3-node reserved mix we expect median token latency to remain within the 95% gate. For the 99th% we estimate a ~18–30% increase vs short requests due to larger KV cache pressure and attention memory; in practice that maps to ~200–300ms for the worst tail on an 800-token session under sustained peak. Recommendation: start pilot with keep-min=1 and a +1 node kept warm for the first 48 hours of peak windows.

2) Cold-start: typical cold-start for a model shard spin-up is 6–9s (cold KV warmup + kernel priming). For user-facing SLAs we recommend keep-min=1 for the pilot and enable aggressive pre-warm for scheduled high-traffic periods. We can also provide an init hook so you measure p95 cold-starts in the pilot.

3) Fallback to quantized variant: expected tail latency delta is +25–60ms per token (varies by sequence length). Quality regression: we run prompt-set based BLEU-like diffs + intent-preservation checks and will surface any >3% semantic delta as a red flag. For the pilot we propose a canary policy: route 100% of low-priority background traffic to the quantized variant for 24h, compare outputs on our eval harness, then allow 5% production fallback if diff <3%.

Ops runbook (summary):
- Pre-pilot (week before): share prompt set + token distribution; Redwood creates pilot pool and runs bench (2–3 hours).
- Day 0: smoke tests (latency profiles, error rates), enable keep-min=1, keep extra node warm for first 48 hours.
- Ongoing: daily SLO digest to your SRE (p50/p95/p99, error rate, fallback count).
- Escalation: Pager -> Redwood on-call (link in Drive doc), then AE escalation to me.

Pilot dates: Jul 11 start works for us. I'll attach a 1-pager ops runbook and the updated SLO matrix by EOD today. DocuSign for the pilot commit will follow if you confirm dates.
